# The appointments Bꜣstt made — and who is keeping them

Take Bꜣstt's stories in sequence. They are not episodes; they are appointments — and the modern trades are keeping them.

## At a Glance

- **Temple:** Bꜣstt
- **Pantheon:** Egyptian
- **Domain of influence:** Home, Fertility, Cats
- **Pattern seats:** 3
- **Sectors touched:** Home & Lifestyle
- **Strongest seat:** Pet Care & Animal Industries
- **Series:** The Resonance Files, No. 80 of 546

## The Cycle, Read Forward

### Pet Care & Animal Industries — through *The Lioness Talked Home*

In the theology of the solar eye, the goddess who is Re's own eye grows angry and abandons Egypt for the Nubian desert, taking leonine form; the sun dims and the land withers behind her.  The gods send the eloquent Thoth — disguised, in the Late Ptolemaic Papyrus Jumilhac, as a baboon — to coax her back with a flood of words and stories.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *She of the ointment jar and the household cat; pet culture’s oldest deity.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. That is the cycle working: story becomes duty, duty becomes trade.

### Home, Hearth & Real Estate — through *Red Beer on the Field of Slaughter*

When humanity plots against the aging Re, the sun-god sends his eye against them, and the eye — a lioness whom later tradition variously names Sekhmet or Bastet — falls upon mankind in a slaughter so complete that even the gods grow afraid the earth will be emptied.  In the version painted on the royal tomb walls of the Book of the Heavenly Cow — Seti I (KV17), Ramesses VI (KV9), and the gilded shrines of Tutankhamun (KV62) — Re halts the carnage with a stratagem: the gods brew seven thousand jars of beer, dye them red with ochre, and flood the fields until the land lies red as blood.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *Home and domestic blessing; the household’s protector.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. Industries do not invent their archetypes; they inherit them and call them best practice.

### Beauty, Fashion & Cosmetics — through *Seven Hundred Thousand Pilgrims*

The fullest account of Bastet's worship was written by a Greek tourist.  Herodotus (Histories 2.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *She of the ointment jar; perfume and cosmetics are in her name.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. Industries do not invent their archetypes; they inherit them and call them best practice.

## The Theme That Runs the Cycle

Bastet's myths are fewer and more fragmented than those of Isis or Horus — Egypt never wrote her a great cycle — but what survives is vivid: the wandering solar eye that must be talked home, the red beer that ends a massacre, and the festival that Herodotus judged the merriest in Egypt.

## The Method, Stated Plainly

None of this is numerology. A seat exists only where the match can be argued from the deity’s documented domains and deeds — weighted, published, and falsifiable. The derivation, the weights, and the challenge process are public on the [methodology page](/patterns/methodology/). If a seat in this file reads wrong, the atlas itself tells you how to prove it — and the correction becomes part of the record.

## For the Ones Who Work There

If you work in pet care & animal industries, home, hearth & real estate, or any trade this temple holds a seat in, this is the honest version of what a placement means: your industry beside the story it has been re-telling all along — on the temple floor itself, before an audience that came specifically to read it. The [patron tier](/bastet/patron/) and the [advertising terms](/terms/advertising/) describe the mechanics; the resonance above describes the fit.
